title: Posting and Availability of Deposits to Savings and Money Market Accounts
content:
### When a deposit posts

Cash, ACH credits, incoming wires and internal or automatic transfers into an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts post on the business day they are received.

A deposited check posts on the next business day. While the account has been open fewer calendar days than the tier's new-account period, however, a deposited check posts on the tier's new-account hold business day after deposit.

### Mobile deposits

A mobile deposit is accepted only where it keeps the day's mobile deposits within the tier's mobile deposit daily limit and the rolling 30 calendar day total of mobile deposits within the tier's mobile deposit limit for that span. A mobile deposit beyond either limit is rejected and never posts.

### Which accounts accept a deposit

Deposits are accepted on active and dormant accounts, and on an applied account as its opening deposit. They are never accepted on a closed account.

### Deposits and dormancy

A deposit is never customer-initiated activity for the purpose of dormancy where it is an ACH credit, an incoming wire or an automatic transfer.

### No longer in force

The clause that made a deposit post on the business day its funds became available, so that the current balance was also the available balance, is no longer in force. It has been superseded, and it is not to be applied to any account of this product.

### Illustration of the new-account hold

Take a hypothetical account opened 10 calendar days ago, whose tier carries a new-account period of 30 calendar days and a hold to the 5th business day after deposit. A check deposited today falls inside the new-account period, so it posts on the 5th business day after the deposit rather than on the next business day. The same check deposited 40 calendar days after opening falls outside that period and posts on the next business day.

superseded_clauses: A deposit posts on the business day its funds become available, so the current balance is also the available balance.
